sentences.text: 4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that initially first information report was lodged on 9.6.2014 and after investigation charge sheet was submitted on 18.9.2016 under Sections 498A, 302, 120B of I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that by means of the impugned order dated 19.5.2025 in exercise of power conferred under Section 311 of the Criminal Procedure Code on an application filed by the State through Public Prosecution, Dr. R.K. Singh has been summoned.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the aforesaid Dr. R.K. Singh has been summoned on the strength of a document produced after medical report dated 23.6.2006 where Dr. R.K. Singh had medically examined the deceased.
The deceased had died in the year 2014.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that after eight years of the previous alleged incident deceased had died and therefore production of new document at this stage when six prosecution witnesses have already been examined would not be in the interest of justice.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the trial court has not recorded any finding with regard to the relevancy of the aforesaid medical report of the year 2006 and the summoning of Dr. R.K. Singh who is alleged to have prepared the medical report.
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that summoning of the aforesaid would delay the trial court proceedings.

5. Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 and learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the applicant and submits that PW-1 in his statement recorded has also referred to the medical report dated 23.06.2006 which was prepared by Dr. R.K. Singh and as a result of the same the aforesaid medical report was brought on record before the trial court and the trial court was pleased to summon Dr. R.K. Singh.
Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 further submits that in terms of Section 311 of Cr.P.C. the trial court has power to call any witness where it is essential for just decision of the case.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and learned A.G.A. further submits that since the cruelty is one of the allegation against the applicant arising out of Section 498-A I.P.C., therefore, in order to demonstrate that cruelty was being subjected to the deceased in the year 2006, the aforesaid document is relevant and the aforesaid document is required to be proved by the witness summoned.
6. It is to be seen that under Section 311 Cr.P.C. the trial court has power to call for any witness where it is essential for just decision of the case.

In the present case as per the informant it has been stated that victim was being regularly subjected to cruelty and as a result of the same in the year Sunil Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190162638/
2 2014 the alleged incident has taken place.

sentences.text: One of the circumstance which the informant in his statement before the trial court is the incident of 2006 where the deceased had given a complaint before the police authorities and she was medically examined where injuries were found.
The gap between the incident of 2006 and 2014 is of about eight years.
It is always open for the prosecution to demonstrate from the record that there was continuous cruelty which the deceased was being subjected prior to her death.
The sole incident of the year 2006 which has been brought on record before the trial court may be one of such incident.
However, at this stage, no finding can be recorded that the aforesaid incident was a continuous event, which is required to be proved by prosecution before the trial court.
Although one incident of the year 2006 may be a material circumstance for the prosecution to demonstrate that previously deceased was also subjected to harassment or cruelty.

7. Be that as it may, once the informant in his statement before the trial court has given details of the medical examination of 23.6.2006 and the aforesaid medical report has been brought on record by the prosecution then summoning of the witness Dr. R.K. Singh to prove the medical report does not in any manner infringe right of the applicant.
8.

At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the aforesaid examination of Dr. R.K.
Singh would lead to delay in the trial as once the aforesaid document is proved, then the applicant would be required to cross examine the already examined prosecution witness.
9. It is to be noted that the accused has always right to cross examine the witness if a document is brought on record.
This right arising out of fair trial which the accused is required to be exercised.
If the summoning of the witness and the document is proved, the accused would always be at liberty to cross examine previous witness by showing the relevancy before the court concerned.

10. At this stage, no interference is warranted in the impugned order and as such the present application under Section 528 BNSS lacks merit and is dismissed subject to right of the applicant to cross examine the previous witness in accordance with law on the new document that may be proved by summoned witness.
(Vikram D. Chauhan,J.) September 2, 2025 VMA  Sunil Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 2 September, 2025
